indices.read: Rolling backtest verdict NO_GO_NO_EDGE - pooled, the next close landed closer to the nearest EOD wall in only 24 of 118 sessions = 20.3% (p vs 50% = 1.0), i.e. walls behaved as ANTI-magnets, markedly worse than a coin flip (SPY 18.6%, QQQ 22.0%). Containment-within-walls and pin-direction were both coin flips at 52.5%. H1 (short-gamma -> higher next-session vol) ran BACKWARDS pooled: long-gamma mean |ret| 0.776 vs short-gamma 0.731 on n=40. Nothing here is a predictive claim. The long-gamma flip is ONE SESSION OLD - SPY was FULLY_NEGATIVE every session 07-27 through 07-30 with a null ZGL throughout, turning POSITIVE with a clean ZGL only at Friday's close, coincident with reclaiming both SMAs. Spot sits almost exactly on both the ZGL (746.93) and the call wall (748), so dealers are near flat-gamma at the money and small moves either way could re-flip the sign. The 2.28% gap down to the 730 put wall is the only real space in the book.
indices.structure_bias: Long-gamma but asymmetric: tight only on the upside (748 vs spot 747.06) while the downside gap to 730 is wide. A condor with the short put leg well inside 730 is more consistent with the book than a tight iron fly, given the flip is unconfirmed and the backtest says the wall is not a floor.
